system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Exxon Mobil (XOM) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Deals of the day-Mergers and acquisitions

BODY:
(Adds: Solventum, Abbott, Enterprise Products Partners, Generali Updates:)

Nov 20 (Reuters) - The following bids, mergers, acquisitions and disposals were reported by 1430 GMT on Thursday:

** Medical device maker Solventum <

SOLV.N

> said it would acquire privately held Acera Surgical for up to $850 million to expand its wound-care portfolio.

** Enterprise Products Partners <

EPD.N

> said that Exxon Mobil <

XOM.N

> will buy a 40% stake in its Bahia natural gas liquids pipeline and help expand the system to handle growing Permian Basin volumes.

** Abbott <

ABT.N

> said it would buy cancer-test maker Exact Sciences <

EXAS.O

> in a deal valued at up to $23 billion, including debt, marking one of its largest acquisitions in nearly a decade and its first major push into cancer screening.

** Insurer Generali <

GAS.MI

>, Milan-listed BFF Bank <

BFF.MI

> and France's BPCE have advanced to the second round of bidding to acquire European life-insurance consolidator GamaLife from Apax Partners, two sources familiar with the matter said.

** Palo Alto Networks said it will buy cloud management and monitoring company Chronosphere for $3.35 billion, as the cybersecurity firm looks to strengthen its AI offerings. (Compiled by Rajarshi Roy and Arnav Mishra in Bengaluru)
</article>

<summary>
Exxon Mobil is set to acquire a 40% stake in Enterprise Products Partners' Bahia natural gas liquids pipeline, partnering to expand the system's capacity to accommodate falling volumes from the Permian Basin. This move reflects Exxon's ongoing strategy to strengthen midstream infrastructure supporting its upstream production growth in one of the most prolific U.S. shale regions. By investing in pipeline capacity, Exxon aims to secure reliable takeaway options for NGLs, potentially improving margins and reducing bottlenecks as Permian output continues to climb, reinforcing its integrated energy value chain.
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article: invented facts,
wrong numbers, wrong direction (e.g. "rose" vs "fell"), wrong company, unattributed rumours stated as fact,
or speculative links to XOM that the article does not make.
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about XOM in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a XOM analyst what matters, and represent how central XOM really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for XOM, and says so plainly if XOM is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the XOM angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores XOM, or implies the article is about / important for XOM when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": ["..."],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
text:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [
    "The expansion is to accommodate 'falling volumes from the Permian Basin'. The article says the expansion is to handle 'growing' Permian volumes, so the summary reverses the direction.",
    "'This move reflects Exxon's ongoing strategy to strengthen midstream infrastructure supporting its upstream production growth.' The article describes no Exxon strategy or rationale.",
    "The Permian is described as 'one of the most prolific U.S. shale regions'. This characterization is not in the article.",
    "'Exxon aims to secure reliable takeaway options for NGLs'. The article attributes no aims or motives to Exxon.",
    "The deal is 'potentially improving margins and reducing bottlenecks'. This is speculative; the article does not mention margins or bottlenecks.",
    "'as Permian output continues to climb'. The article says only 'growing Permian Basin volumes'. This line also contradicts the summary's own 'falling volumes' claim.",
    "'reinforcing its integrated energy value chain'. This is a speculative strategic interpretation that the article does not make."
  ],
  "missing_key_facts": [
    "The announcement came from Enterprise Products Partners (EPD), not Exxon. The summary gives no attribution.",
    "The expansion is driven by growing Permian Basin volumes. The summary misstates this as falling volumes.",
    "No deal value or financial terms were disclosed. The item is a brief entry in a multi-deal roundup with no further detail on Exxon."
  ],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true,
  "faithfulness": 2,
  "ticker_focus": 3,
  "coverage": 3,
  "conciseness": 2
}
